news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics CFO Louis Tamayo Sells 4,641 Shares
news.summary: CFO Louis Tamayo sold 4,641 shares at a weighted-average price of $4.49 on July 1, 2026, to cover tax withholding on RSUs that vested on June 29; CEO Nolan Townsend made a similar tax-related sale of 25,947 shares at $4.48 the same day. Both were routine, pre-scheduled equity-compensation transactions tied to RSU vesting rather than discretionary open-market sales.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics CEO and CFO Receive Restricted Stock Unit Awards
news.summary: CEO Nolan Townsend was granted 67,000 shares of common stock as a performance/time-based compensation award, with CFO Louis Tamayo receiving a smaller 12,000-share award on the same date, June 29, 2026.

news.headline: JPMorgan Cuts Lexeo Therapeutics Price Target to $9 from $12, Maintains Overweight
news.summary: JPMorgan trimmed its LXEO price target to $9 from $12 while reiterating an Overweight rating, citing an updated valuation model following recent pipeline developments; separately, Weiss Ratings held its rating at the low end of its scale (Sell E+), underscoring a split analyst picture.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics Holds 2026 Virtual Annual Meeting, Elects Directors and Ratifies KPMG
news.summary: At its fully virtual 2026 annual stockholders meeting, Lexeo shareholders elected three Class III directors to terms running through 2029 and ratified KPMG LLP as the company's independent registered public accounting firm.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics Announces Publication in JAMA Cardiology of Phase I/II Data for LX2006 in Friedreich Ataxia
news.summary: Peer-reviewed Phase I/II data on 17 Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy patients treated with LX2006 showed sustained cardiac and neurologic improvements, favorable biomarker changes, and a generally well-tolerated safety profile, reinforcing the clinical rationale behind the pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 program.

news.headline: Lexeo Therapeutics Announces Regulatory Update and Registrational Trial Design for LX2006 Gene Therapy in Friedreich Ataxia
news.summary: Lexeo finalized with the FDA the pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 trial protocol and statistical analysis plan for LX2006, confirmed it can use its optimized Sf9-baculovirus commercial-scale manufacturing process for dosing, and targeted a BLA submission under the accelerated approval pathway in H1 2028; enrollment of the first patient was expected by end of June 2026, and shares jumped nearly 13% on the news.

catalysts.label: Q2 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: Lexeo is expected to report second-quarter 2026 financial results and pipeline updates in August 2026 (it reported Q2 2025 results on August 14, 2025); an exact 2026 date has not yet been announced.

catalysts.label: LX2020 12-month high-dose data (HEROIC-PKP2)
catalysts.detail: Company guidance calls for a 12-month data update covering all high-dose PKP2-associated arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy participants in the ongoing HEROIC-PKP2 Phase I/II trial.

catalysts.label: SUNRISE-FA2 topline data readout
catalysts.detail: Topline data from the pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 trial of LX2006 in Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy is guided for the second half of 2027.

catalysts.label: LX2006 BLA submission
catalysts.detail: Lexeo plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the FDA for LX2006 under the accelerated approval pathway in the first half of 2028.

catalysts.label: First patient dosed in pivotal SUNRISE-FA2 trial
catalysts.detail: Following the June 2026 FDA-aligned trial design finalization, Lexeo guided to enrolling the first SUNRISE-FA2 pivotal-trial participant by the end of June 2026; confirmation of actual first dosing has not yet been separately announced.

pulse: Lexeo remains a clinical-stage cardiovascular gene therapy company advancing two lead AAV programs, LX2006 for Friedreich ataxia cardiomyopathy and LX2020 for PKP2-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, having finalized the FDA-aligned SUNRISE-FA2 pivotal trial design in mid-June 2026 (sending shares up nearly 13%) and followed that with supportive LX2006 data published in JAMA Cardiology days later. Since then the news flow has gone quiet, limited mostly to routine insider RSU grants/tax-related sales and a June 25 annual meeting, while JPMorgan trimmed its price target to $9 (from $12, still Overweight) the same day Weiss Ratings kept a Sell-grade view, and the stock has traded rangebound in the mid-single digits (roughly $4.50-$5.50) through late July after having fallen sharply from a 52-week high near $11. With cash guided to last into 2028 (following a ~15% workforce reduction earlier in 2026 to focus resources on the cardiac pipeline), the next concrete catalysts are Q2 2026 earnings expected in August, confirmation of first-patient dosing in SUNRISE-FA2, 12-month high-dose LX2020 data in Q4 2026, and SUNRISE-FA2 topline data in H2 2027 ahead of a planned 2028 BLA filing.
